new_scholarship.name: John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship
new_scholarship.duration: Up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course; a maximum of 2 years for a Master's degree by coursework. Curtin calls this the 'Scholarship term'.
new_scholarship.deadline: The scholarship page states 'Applications open: 27/07/2026' and 'Applications close: 1/10/2027'. Curtin uses day/month/year on this page, so these are 27 July 2026 and 1 October 2027. Curtin adds: 'Curtin reserves the right to cease offering this Scholarship if you do not accept by the due date stated on the Letter of Offer OR when all the Scholarship places are filled.'
new_scholarship.application_period: Applications to the scholarship are open from 27 July 2026 until 1 October 2027 for students commencing at a Curtin Western Australian campus in 2027 or 2028. Because there is no separate scholarship application, the scholarship window is governed by the Curtin course application, which runs on Curtin's Semester 1 (February) and Semester 2 (July) intakes with different closing dates per course.
application_method: Automatic on admission to the course, not a separate scholarship application. The page states: 'There is no separate scholarship application required.'
Apply for the Curtin course either through one of Curtin University registered education agents or by applying directly to Curtin online.
'All qualifying applications to Curtin are automatically assessed for the John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship.'
Global Admissions assesses each application and issues a supplementary letter, along with a Letter of Offer, to confirm whether the applicant has been successful.
To accept the scholarship offer you must pay the full Deposit amount set out in your Letter of Offer for the first study period of your Course.
new_scholarship.description: The John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based award funded by Curtin University for international, fee-paying, non-sponsored students enrolling in an eligible undergraduate degree or Master degree by coursework at a Curtin Western Australian campus, commencing in 2027 or 2028. Eligible students receive 40% off the tuition fee of their course, credited against all units enrolled within the scholarship term, which runs for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master's degree by coursework. Curtin states that the scholarship 'Only covers tuition fees and does not cover any other international student expense', is credited to the recipient's fee account after the census date of the first study period, and cannot be withdrawn or refunded in cash. There is no separate scholarship application: every qualifying application to Curtin is assessed automatically and the outcome is confirmed by a supplementary letter issued with the Letter of Offer.
new_scholarship.best_fit: International students of any nationality except Australian, who are not sponsored and are paying full international fees, hold a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in their most recent eligible study, and are applying to an eligible Curtin WA campus undergraduate degree or coursework master's for a 2027 or 2028 commencement.

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: The scholarship is only for international, fee-paying, non-sponsored students of any nationality except Australian who are enrolled in a Curtin undergraduate degree course or a Master degree by coursework, will be studying at a Curtin Western Australian campus commencing in 2027 or 2028, and have achieved a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent scores in their most recent and eligible course of study. Applicants must not be enrolled in a Not-for-Degree Exchange or Study Abroad program, must not be a campus transfer from a Curtin global campus, and must not be in a recognised joint program at a Curtin Transnational Partner Location outside Australia. Curtin determines the CWA and the list of excluded courses and may change both without notice.

new_scholarship.english_requirement: The scholarship page itself publishes no English requirement of its own. The underlying Curtin course admission imposes Curtin's minimum English standard: IELTS Academic or IELTS UKVI overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0 (Listening 6.0, Reading 6.0, Writing 6.0, Speaking 6.0), or Pearson Test of English overall 58 with Listening 50, Reading 50, Writing 51 and Speaking 54 for tests taken from August 2026 (50 in each component for tests taken before August 2026). TOEFL iBT from June 2026 requires Reading 16, Listening 16, Speaking 19, Writing 19, overall 81. The test must have been undertaken within two years of application, results from multiple tests are not combined, and some courses have specific higher English requirements that these minimum scores do not satisfy.
new_scholarship.selection_notes: There is no separate application or separate selection panel. Curtin states that 'All qualifying applications to Curtin are automatically assessed for the John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship' and that Global Admissions will assess each application accordingly and issue a supplementary letter with the Letter of Offer to confirm whether the applicant has been successful. The published academic threshold for entry is a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in the most recent and eligible course of study, which Curtin determines and may change without notice. No selection weighting, panel, interview or shortlisting process is published. Curtin reserves the right to cease offering the Scholarship when all Scholarship places are filled, so the published closing date is not a guarantee that places remain.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: Annual award, named by commencement year. Applications for the scholarship are open from 27 July 2026 and close on 1 October 2027, and the scholarship is awarded for study commencing in 2027 or 2028 at a Curtin Western Australian campus. Because there is no separate scholarship application, candidates apply on the Curtin course application cycle for the relevant intake.
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: Applications close 1/10/2027 (Curtin day/month/year format, so 1 October 2027), with applications opening 27/07/2026 (27 July 2026). Curtin publishes no time of day for this closing date.
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: This is the scholarship's own published closing date and it is exact: 1 October 2027, Australia/Perth (AWST, UTC+8). No time of day is published, so deadline_precision is 'day'. Two caveats are recorded rather than resolved. First, Curtin reserves the right to cease offering the Scholarship when all Scholarship places are filled, so the published date is not a guarantee that a place remains. Second, because assessment is automatic on the Curtin course application, the binding constraint for any individual applicant is the course application closing date for the chosen intake, which differs by course and by intake. The Curtin application deadlines page was read but it served the domestic visitor view, in which Semester 1 2027 applications 'opened on Friday 1 May 2026, and will close for most courses on Thursday 28 January 2027'. The international-view deadline for the specific intake a non-domestic applicant would use was therefore not captured, so no institutional deadline is asserted here.

programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a tuition fee reduction and does cover tuition fees, but only partially: 40% off the tuition fee of the course, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master's degree by coursework, against all units enrolled within the scholarship term. Curtin is explicit that it 'Only covers tuition fees and does not cover any other international student expense', so the recipient still pays the remaining 60% of tuition fees plus the full Deposit stated in the Letter of Offer. It is also explicit that the award 'Cannot be withdrawn or refunded in cash' and cannot be transferred to a Curtin campus or partner outside Western Australia or to another university. Because it is tuition-only and leaves 60% of tuition and all living costs payable, fully_funded is false.

programme_detail_official.description: The John Curtin Global Excellence Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship funded by Curtin University. Eligible students receive 40% off the tuition fee of the course they are undertaking, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master degree by coursework, as a tuition fee credit against all units enrolled within the course within the scholarship term. It is open to international, fee-paying, non-sponsored students of any nationality except Australian who will study at a Curtin Western Australian campus commencing in 2027 or 2028, and who have achieved a Course-Weighted Average of 95% or equivalent in their most recent and eligible course of study. The scholarship is credited to the recipient's fee account after the census date of the first study period, only covers tuition fees, and cannot be withdrawn or refunded in cash. There is no separate scholarship application: all qualifying applications to Curtin are assessed automatically and Global Admissions confirms the outcome by issuing a supplementary letter with the Letter of Offer.
programme_detail_official.coverage: 40% of the tuition fee of the course, credited for up to 4 years for an undergraduate degree course or a maximum of 2 years for a Master degree by coursework. Tuition fees only; no living cost, accommodation, travel or other international student expense is covered.

alerts.message: Six undergraduate degrees are excluded: Bachelor of Science (Medical Radiation Science), Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery, Bachelor of Science (Advanced Nursing), Bachelor of Science (Paramedicine), and Bachelor of Science (Oral Health Therapy). If you are heading into medicine, surgery, nursing, paramedicine, oral health or medical radiation science, this scholarship is very likely not available to you. Curtin also states the excluded list may change without notice, so re-check it in your application year.

alerts.trigger: Before you submit your Curtin course application
alerts.message: Confirm you are international, fee-paying and non-sponsored, and that you hold no other Curtin or Australian Government scholarship. Any one of those disqualifies you.
Pay the full Deposit for the first study period. Until you do, the scholarship is not accepted, and the 40% will not reduce that deposit. Make sure you can fund it yourself.

The published closing date is 1 October 2027, but Curtin reserves the right to cease offering the Scholarship when all places are filled. Apply in the first study period you are eligible for rather than waiting.

alerts.trigger: If your English test is more than two years old
alerts.message: Curtin requires the English test to have been undertaken within two years of application, and does not combine results from multiple tests. Book a new sitting rather than relying on an old score.
Hold 'Good Standing' and a minimum CWA of 70% from the second study period onwards, in every study period. Both are conditions, and failing either can revoke the scholarship.

alerts.trigger: If you are considering deferral or Leave of Absence
alerts.message: Neither preserves the award. Deferring beyond the offered study period and year ends eligibility, and Leave of Absence study periods still count against your scholarship term.

alerts.trigger: If you are considering a course change
alerts.message: Curtin reassesses eligibility in the new course. Moving into or out of an excluded degree can end the award and leave you with outstanding tuition fees.
